summary: w03 is safe and readable, and most lines are short, child-friendly and built on genuinely real animal facts (indigo buntings steering by stars, turnstones flipping stones, crows using traffic to crack nuts, dipper walking underwater, hawk screech dubbed for eagles, betta bubble nests, puffin fish moustache, aquarium filter humming a note under the fridge). The biggest weakness is structural: about thirty objects scale one signature trait across three to five rarities (cockatoo bins, turnstone stones, ouzel underwater walking, redshank alarms, spoonbill stirring, dowitcher probing, jacamar butterflies, ptarmigan camouflage, egret stillness, black stork shyness), so the ladders feel like one joke with bigger numbers. Second, close relatives are often interchangeable: eagle/bald eagle (nest E and soaring L), egret C = heron U, kingfisher L = little blue heron L, coho L = salmon L, duck/duckling/coot traffic and pond-boss lines, crow E = raven E, African grey/parrot/starling mimicry, black grouse E = prairie chicken E word for word, whale C = grey whale U, rock beauty and angelfish sharing 'Coral Catwalk'. Third, Epics lean on one template ('Led a parade/flock of N...', about 29 crowd Epics), and Legendaries cluster around migration-homecoming, longevity and 'became famous/official', with many lacking a punchline (whale shark, coral, white stork, goldfish bowl, fish). Hard flags: a brand name (bee eater 'Melitta'), a trademarked character on a move (falcon 'Hawkeye Glare'), a biblical name (hummingbird 'Zippora'), death or cooking jokes (prawn pink in hot water, salmon seeing relatives in sushi, vulture circling tired people, cod 'Batterhopeful'), a film-plot and flushing echo (fish E), a w01 punchline copy (pelican 'fishermen... sandwiches'), a cold word on a burn move (narwhal 'Icy Tusk Burn'), and fact slips (bustard as a poor flier, glowing starfish, manta 'sting', gar older than the dinosaurs, slow sea turtle, century-old grey whale). Monster names are paired with the wrong rarity's lore in about 50 objects (mostly adjacent swaps), the same defect w02 had; concrete re-pairings are given. Move mechanics are mostly respected: drain, heal, buff and multi-hit names fit, and most variant-differing Ultimates are effect-neutral. The fixes are cold words on burn Ultimates (junco, ptarmigan, narwhal), three Ultimates identical to the Epic name, 'Thinking Pulse' on a 3-hit move, 'Shut Tight' on a defence-down move, and a few near-collisions with kit moves. Every high and medium item has a drop-in replacement.

patterns.pattern: Epic template: 'Led a parade/flock/line/run/shoal/dance of N...' opens 20 Epics, plus 'Arrived with a flock so...' (4) and 'with a hundred/fifty/ten thousand friends' (5). That is about a quarter of all Epics on one frame. Many end in 'the whole sky/lake/park turned X'.
patterns.suggestion: Keep at most 5 crowd Epics in the batch. Give the others one creature causing one concrete disaster (see the per-object replacements). Drop 'the whole sky turned...' (brambling, macaw, stork, starling) to one use.

patterns.pattern: One headline trait scaled across three to five rarities instead of five premises (the commonest problem in this batch).
patterns.suggestion: Let the signature trait own at most two rarities and use other real traits (nest, diet, body, family life, famous fact) for the rest. Replacements are in the issues list.

patterns.pattern: Close relatives share premises, so their lore is interchangeable.
patterns.suggestion: Pairs that collide: eagle/bald eagle (nest E, soaring L), egret C/heron U (garden ornament), kingfisher L/little blue heron L (fish in every river/pond in one day), coho L/salmon L (homing), duck U+E/duckling E (traffic-stopping line), duck L/coot L (pond boss, bread queue), crow E/raven E ('Organised every X into a gang'), African grey U/parrot E (embarrassing words), African grey R/starling R (doorbell), macaw R/indigo bunting C ('painted'), black grouse E/prairie chicken E (dance-off), whale C/grey whale U (spout timing), rock beauty/angelfish (Coral Catwalk), dowitcher E/kiwi E (holes), dowitcher U/sandpiper C (wave running), crane C/flamingo C+L (one leg), stork R/albatross R (no flap). The issues list says which side to change.

patterns.pattern: Rare template: 'struck/snapped a fish so fast that the fish didn't notice'.
patterns.suggestion: Keep heron R (splash after swallowing) and little blue heron R; rewrite the other three (replacements given).

patterns.pattern: Legendary clusters. (a) Migration/homecoming ('flew around the world, landed on the same beach/field/barn'). (b) Longevity ('lived N years and remembers everyone'). (c) 'Became the official/symbol/most famous...' (12 Legendaries start with 'Became').
patterns.suggestion: No more than 3 to 4 of each shape per batch. Migration stays for the swallow, eel, salmon and sea turtle, where it is iconic; albatross, sandpiper, stork, coho and grey whale get other premises (several replacements given). Prefer an achievement with a twist ('Is a cuckoo that actually raises its own chicks...') over 'became famous'.

patterns.pattern: Lines that state a true fact with no comic consequence (no punchline). Common in Legendaries.
patterns.suggestion: Each line needs a concrete reaction (a person, place or thing that responds). The real facts are good material, so keep them as setups and add the turn, as in the replacements.

patterns.pattern: Dawn noise Commons: screeching or singing at sunrise opens many bird ladders.
patterns.suggestion: Keep it for the canary (cover off the cage) and macaw at most; replacements are given for the sulphur-crested cockatoo, bulbul and others.

patterns.pattern: Monster names paired with the wrong rarity's lore (the same defect w02 had): often a swap of two adjacent names, sometimes a rotation of three.
patterns.suggestion: Re-pair names to their own rarity's line (concrete names are given per object). Whenever a lore line is replaced from this review, re-check that rarity's name; several replacement names here already target the new lines.

patterns.pattern: Name formulas and repeated name stems. Legendary titles: Lady ×5, Old ×4, Professor ×3, Captain ×3, Sir ×2, Grand ×2, Admiral (duck epithet and penguin), Commander (coot), Queen (hornbill); 103 of 120 Legendaries carry a ', the ...' or 'of the ...' epithet. Stems: 'Rainbow' in about 12 names; 'Raider' in 3 Epics (Lake/Hive/Reef Raider); 'Bigbeak' (hornbill R, macaw R); 'Redlegs' (redshank C, stork U); 'Chip-' (bird, seagull); 'Coral Catwalk' (rock beauty, angelfish); 'Drum' names for the ruffed grouse and woodpecker (Forest Drumroll / Forest Drum Solo, Drummond, the Forest Drummer / Picus, the Hammering Drummer).
patterns.suggestion: Cap each title word at 2 per batch and let about a third of Legendaries go without an epithet. Rename one of each stem pair (concrete names are in the issues list). Woodpecker E could become 'Shed Ventilator' and its L 'Picus, Window Fitter of the Oak'.

patterns.pattern: Move-name formulas: heals are 'X Rest' (15 times), defence-down legend moves are 'X Distraction' (6) or 'X Muddle' (5), and almost every Ultimate is the Epic monster name plus Swoop/Surge/Rush/Strike (3 are identical to the Epic name). Clash-avoiding suffixes were bolted on ('Splash Dive Duck', 'Riverbank Rest Goose', 'Shell Brace Turtle').
patterns.suggestion: Vary the heal words (patch, refill, preen, nap, dry off) and the defence-down words (crack, soften, unravel, ruffle). Give Ultimates their own image rather than echoing the Epic name.

patterns.pattern: Cross-batch and in-batch repeated punchlines and props: fishermen (10 lines), sunglasses (ostrich L, parakeet L, salmon E), ferry (dolphin R/E, cod E, orca E), thank-you card (limpkin L, electric ray L, plus w01/w02), 'in the land' (duck L, fish L, spoonbill L; 10 times in w01/w02), 'in one afternoon/morning/day' (21 lines), rent (anemone U, coral U, woodpecker L), 'thought a storm/cloud had arrived' (coot E, sandpiper E, manta E), weddings (cockatoo E, peacock E), dance-offs and festivals (black grouse, prairie chicken, bulbul, ruffed grouse), pelican E vs w01 'fishermen having sandwiches for tea'.
patterns.suggestion: Use each prop and punchline once per batch. Replacements in the issues list already remove most of the duplicates.

patterns.pattern: Sentence engine 'so X that...' appears in 119 of 600 lines; together with 'every X in the Y' (36) it makes the batch read uniformly.
patterns.suggestion: Vary the shape: a plain action plus a deadpan second sentence, a claim plus a deflation ('Says it is waiting for fashion to come back round'), or an attitude line.

issues.issue: 'Melitta' is a well-known coffee-filter brand.
issues.suggestion: 'Waggle, Bane of the Busy Bee'

issues.issue: 'Hawkeye' is a trademarked comic-book character name (and names the wrong bird). Mechanic: stun 30%.
issues.suggestion: 'Peregrine Flash' (flash = stun word).

issues.issue: Turning pink in hot water means being cooked alive: a death/cruelty joke for a child audience.
issues.suggestion: 'Is so see-through that you can watch its breakfast going down. It really wishes you would look away.'

issues.issue: Seeing its relatives in sushi rolls at the fish counter is a death/eating joke.
issues.suggestion: 'Turns up at the river mouth every autumn and waits for the tide like it is queuing for a bus.'

issues.issue: 'Icy' is a cold word on a burn move (100% · burn 40%).
issues.suggestion: 'Sizzling Tusk'

issues.issue: Repeats the w01 punchline almost word for word ('The fishermen are having sandwiches for tea'); 'in one afternoon' is also a batch-wide frame.
issues.suggestion: 'Herded the fish into the shallows with fifty friends in a perfect horseshoe. The harbour master has asked them to run the fishing fleet.' (real cooperative fishing)

issues.issue: 'Zippora' reads as the biblical name Zipporah (a religious figure).
issues.suggestion: 'Zipzing, the Humming Jewel'

issues.issue: 'Roadrunner' is another real bird and a famous cartoon character; confusing on a pheasant.
issues.suggestion: 'Lanedasher'

issues.issue: 'the chief's soup' risks a tribal-chief stereotype in a jungle setting.
issues.suggestion: 'Flipped a mango into the air, caught it, and flicked the stone straight into the zookeeper's tea.'

issues.issue: Bowl, bath, drain, sea is the plot of a famous animated film, and it nudges children towards flushing pet fish.
issues.suggestion: 'Jumped out of its bowl into the big tank next door and declared itself the new boss. The angelfish take turns to complain.'

issues.issue: Circling 'whenever someone looks slightly tired' means waiting for someone to die: a death joke. It is also the same premise as the Epic.
issues.suggestion: 'Spreads its huge wings in the morning sun to warm up, as if it is waiting for a round of applause.' (real sunning posture)

issues.issue: Same premise as the Common (circling until animals worry they are dying), with the same death implication.
issues.suggestion: 'Rode one warm air current with fifty friends, and the hot-air balloons had to queue behind them.'

issues.issue: 'Circlewaiter' keeps the waiting-for-death idea; once the Common changes it no longer matches either.
issues.suggestion: 'Sunspreader'

issues.issue: Manta rays have no stinging barb (that is the stingray). Mechanic: poison 50%.
issues.suggestion: 'Slimy Wing Swipe'

issues.issue: Wrong fact: great bustards are strong fliers. They are heavy, but they do not land a few metres after take-off. The Legendary repeats the same 'bad flier' idea.
issues.suggestion: 'Walks everywhere very slowly to save energy, and is deeply offended whenever a hare overtakes it.'

issues.issue: Same 'can barely fly' premise as the Common, and it contradicts the Rare (one of the heaviest birds that flies well).
issues.suggestion: 'Took off at one end of the plain and landed at the other. The ground has asked for some warning next time.'

issues.issue: Repeats the Uncommon (puffing up its feathers), and the linter flags cosmic scale below Legendary ('blocked out the sun').
issues.suggestion: 'Landed on the village cricket pitch with such a thump that the bails fell off at both ends.'

issues.issue: Wrong fact: starfish do not glow or guide sailors. It is a star pun with no joke.
issues.suggestion: 'Grew a whole new starfish from one lost arm. The two of them still argue about which one is the original.' (real for some species)

issues.issue: Regrowing an arm is the Legendary's trait (after the fix); give the Uncommon another real trait.
issues.suggestion: 'Has a tiny eye at the tip of every arm, so it always knows who is sneaking up, from any direction.'

issues.issue: 'Fiveharm' reads as 'five harm', probably a typo for Fivearm.
issues.suggestion: 'Fivearm'

issues.issue: Gars did not exist 'before the dinosaurs' (they appear later); 'according to the fish' does not save it.
issues.suggestion: 'Has looked exactly the same for a hundred million years, and says it is waiting for fashion to come back round.'

issues.issue: Grey whales do not live for a century, and the line has no punchline.
issues.suggestion: 'Swims from the icy north to the warm south and back every year, and still gets grumpy if another whale is in its favourite lagoon.'

issues.issue: Sea turtles are not slow swimmers (that is the land tortoise).
issues.suggestion: 'Naps on the reef for so long between swims that the fish have opened a little cafe on its shell.'

issues.issue: Bald eagles do not nap while soaring. The albatross Rare uses the same idea, and the line has no punchline.
issues.suggestion: 'Has a fierce face but a squeaky little call, so it glares extra hard to make up for it.'

issues.issue: 'Liberty' ties the bird to its role as a national emblem (political overtone); 'Lord of Skies' is a stock title.
issues.suggestion: 'Whitehead, Keeper of the Lake'

issues.issue: 'Snowfield' is a cold word on an all-burn Ultimate.
issues.suggestion: 'Sunny Hedge Scorch'

issues.issue: 'Whiteout' is a snow/cold word, but the spectral and mutated variants burn; it needs an effect-neutral name.
issues.suggestion: 'Mountain Mischief Storm'

issues.issue: Identical to the Epic monster name, and 'Arctic' is cold while the spectral variant burns.
issues.suggestion: 'Tusk Twirl Showdown'

issues.issue: Identical to the Epic monster name 'Midnight Hoot Choir'.
issues.suggestion: 'Midnight Hoot Ambush'

issues.issue: Identical to the Epic monster name 'Country Lane Chaos'.
issues.suggestion: 'Hedgerow Hullabaloo'

issues.issue: The move hits 3 times (45% ×3), but 'Thinking Pulse' sounds like one blow.
issues.suggestion: 'Think Think Think'

issues.issue: Poison move (90% · poison 50%); 'Gulp' suggests drain, not poison.
issues.suggestion: 'Stale Plankton Burp'

issues.issue: 'Shut Tight' sounds like a self-defence brace, but the move lowers the enemy's defence (60% · defdown 70%).
issues.suggestion: 'Grit in the Eye'

issues.issue: 'Fin Slap Splash' nearly collides with this fish's own kit move 'Fin Slap' (Epic).
issues.suggestion: 'Bowl Splash'

issues.issue: 'Flicking Tail' nearly collides with the signature 'Tail Flick Slap'.
issues.suggestion: 'Antenna Whip'

issues.issue: 'Tentacle Swipe' nearly collides with the signature 'Tentacle Slap'.
issues.suggestion: 'Frond Swipe'

issues.issue: 'Shell Clap' nearly collides with the signature 'Shell Snap'.
issues.suggestion: 'Clam Clout'

issues.issue: 'Squelch Slap' is very close to the signature 'Soggy Slap'.
issues.suggestion: 'Squelch Bump'

issues.issue: 'Goose' looks bolted on to avoid a name clash; it reads badly.
issues.suggestion: 'Down Feather Nap'

issues.issue: 'Duck' looks bolted on to avoid a name clash.
issues.suggestion: 'Dabble Dive'

issues.issue: 'Turtle' looks bolted on to avoid a name clash (with the prawn's 'Shell Brace').
issues.suggestion: 'Shell Tuck'

issues.issue: 'Drum Roll' suggests a multi-hit, but the Ultimate is a single 210% blow.
issues.suggestion: 'Marsh Booming Blast'

issues.issue: 'Drumroll' suggests a multi-hit, but the Ultimate is a single 210% blow.
issues.suggestion: 'Log Thunder Blast'

issues.issue: 'Flurry' suggests several hits on a single-hit defence-down move; at 26 characters it is also near the limit.
issues.suggestion: 'Ruffled Feathers'

issues.issue: 'Nose Bump' does not suggest poison (poison 50%). The id is dolphin.
issues.suggestion: 'Fishy Breath Bump' (or keep: it is not contradictory)

issues.issue: The Bible uses 'Flash' for stun; this move lowers defence.
issues.suggestion: 'Glinting Wing Distraction'

issues.issue: 'Shadowy' is an odd word for one of the brightest birds alive.
issues.suggestion: 'Rainbow Feint'

issues.issue: Interchangeable with bald eagle E (a cliff nest so big it looks like a hut or a house).
issues.suggestion: 'Flapped once over the ski slope, and every skier went down the mountain twice as fast as they meant to.'

issues.issue: Interchangeable with bald eagle L (soared so high it saw tomorrow's weather / two sunrises).
issues.suggestion: 'Has been drawn on so many flags and shields that it now refuses to be painted from its bad side.'

issues.issue: Same premise as eagle R (snatching a fish from a rival), and the salmon-and-bear scene is also in coho R and E.
issues.suggestion: 'Only gets its white head at five years old, and spends the years before that insisting it is not a teenager.'

issues.issue: Same premise as the Legendary (films borrowing its screech for other birds). Keep the Legendary, which is the stronger line.
issues.suggestion: 'Has a brick-red tail and flicks it like a cape every time it lands on a fence post.'

issues.issue: Repeats the Common (circling overhead), just over a motorway.
issues.suggestion: 'Circled above the school sports day so long that every child ran the egg-and-spoon race looking up.'

issues.issue: 'Harrier' is a different bird of prey and 'Haunted' has nothing to do with the lore.
issues.suggestion: 'Screecher Supreme, Voice of Every Eagle'

issues.issue: 'Thermalrider' does not match the Uncommon lore (screech, now the red tail).
issues.suggestion: 'Redcape'

issues.issue: Identical premise to heron U (stands so still that people think it is a garden ornament). Stillness also returns in the Epic and the Legendary.
issues.suggestion: 'Stands perfectly still in the pond for so long that people think it is a garden ornament.' (keep here; heron U changes instead, see below)

issues.issue: Third stillness premise for this object (Common, Epic and Legendary).
issues.suggestion: 'Shuffled its feet in the shallows so hard that every fish in the marsh shot onto the bank and asked for a towel.' (real foot-stirring)

issues.issue: Fourth stillness line ('standing perfectly still through a hurricane'), and 'became the symbol of' is a batch-wide frame.
issues.suggestion: 'Grew such magnificent white plumes that every swan on the lake booked a hairdresser.'

issues.issue: The 'struck a fish so fast' Rare is shared with heron, little blue heron, gar and barracouta.
issues.suggestion: 'Tosses every fish in the air to swallow it head-first. Misses about once a week and calls it a juggling trick.'

issues.issue: 'Fishstatue' describes stillness, but the Rare lore is a fast strike (now the fish toss).
issues.suggestion: 'Fishjuggler'

issues.issue: Identical premise to egret C (mistaken for a garden ornament).
issues.suggestion: 'Flies with its neck folded into an S, so it always looks like it has just remembered something embarrassing.'

issues.issue: 'Statuestand' matches the old line; after the fix it no longer fits.
issues.suggestion: 'Foldneck'

issues.issue: 'Stalked so patiently' copies heron L (patience pays off).
issues.suggestion: 'Waded into the town fountain and fished so calmly that tourists threw coins at it. It has bought itself a very small boat.'

issues.issue: 'Slowstepper' does not match the Uncommon lore (white turning blue).
issues.suggestion: 'Whitetoblue'

issues.issue: Interchangeable with little blue heron L (caught a fish in every river/pond in the county in one day).
issues.suggestion: 'Dug a tunnel into the riverbank so long that it came out in the village bakery. It now dives for doughnuts.' (real burrow nester)

issues.issue: A true fact with no chaos and no punchline (copied for a train nose).
issues.suggestion: 'Dived so cleanly that engineers copied its beak for a high-speed train. Now it races the train every morning and wins.'

issues.issue: Shares the 'snapped a fish so fast' Rare with egret, heron, little blue heron and barracouta.
issues.suggestion: 'Gulps air at the surface so loudly that anglers spin round looking for whoever burped.' (gars breathe air)

issues.issue: Shares the 'snapped a fish so fast' Rare; speed also fills the Uncommon, Epic and Legendary.
issues.suggestion: 'Bites straight through fishing line, then hangs around the boat to see whether you have any more.'

issues.issue: Third speed premise (Uncommon, Epic and Legendary all say 'very fast').
issues.suggestion: 'Followed a fishing boat all the way into harbour and tried to buy a ticket for the return trip.'

issues.issue: Interchangeable with salmon L (swims home to the exact place it was born). Coho is a salmon, so it needs its own traits.
issues.suggestion: 'Turned such a bright red for its journey home that the lighthouse switched off and let the coho do the job.' (coho turn red with a hooked jaw)

issues.issue: Bears again (Rare and Epic), and bears also appear in bald eagle R; 'Led a run of a thousand' is the batch Epic template.
issues.suggestion: 'Jumped so many waterfalls in one week that the river put up a sign saying PLEASE USE THE STAIRS.'

issues.issue: Homing by smell is the same premise as its Legendary (found the exact pebble where it hatched).
issues.suggestion: 'Was born in a river, grew up in the sea, and still complains that the sea is far too salty.'

issues.issue: 'Led a shoal' template plus 'sunglasses' (also in ostrich L and parakeet L).
issues.suggestion: 'Leapt up the salmon ladder so fast that the fish counter at the dam ran out of numbers.'

issues.issue: 'Homesniffer' describes homing, not the Common line.
issues.suggestion: 'Tidequeuer'

issues.issue: 'Rainbowtrout' is just the species label.
issues.suggestion: 'Shimmerstripe'

issues.issue: Repeats the Common (dodging anglers and hooks).
issues.suggestion: 'Swam up the waterfall into the mountain lake and has been its only fish for so long that it thinks it invented water.'

issues.issue: A leaping-away-from-fishers Rare like salmon R and coho R; fine on its own, repetitive in the family.
issues.suggestion: 'Leapt clean over the angler's net and splashed back right behind him.' (keep, or swap to another trait)

issues.issue: Bins in Uncommon, Rare, Epic and Legendary: one trait scaled up.
issues.suggestion: 'Chewed through every wooden balcony railing on the street in one week. The builders now arrive with metal ones and a nervous look.'

issues.issue: Same bin premise as the Rare, just country-wide; 'the government' also brushes politics.
issues.suggestion: 'Lived past a hundred, outlasting three owners, two houses and every bin lid ever designed to stop it.'

issues.issue: A fourth bin line.
issues.suggestion: 'Raises its yellow crest when it is excited, so the whole street knows it has found something it should not have.'

issues.issue: 'Binlidder' describes the Rare (bin lids), not the Common (dawn screech).
issues.suggestion: 'Sunrise Shrieker'

issues.issue: Dawn screeching is shared with the macaw, lorikeet, bulbul and canary Commons.
issues.suggestion: 'Hangs upside down from the gutter to stare in at breakfast, then screams when nobody shares.'

issues.issue: Dancing in the Uncommon, Epic and Legendary.
issues.suggestion: 'Unscrewed every handle in the kitchen while the family slept. Breakfast took an hour to get into.'

issues.issue: Third dancing line ('danced every night for eighty years').
issues.suggestion: 'Gives off so much fine feather dust that the whole house looks freshly floured. The bakery next door asked for the recipe.' (real powder-down)

issues.issue: 'Cuddlebeak' matches the Common (cuddles), not the Uncommon (dancing).
issues.suggestion: 'Beatbobber'

issues.issue: 'Crestdancer' matches the Uncommon/Rare, not the Common.
issues.suggestion: 'Cuddlescreech'

issues.issue: Same premise as the Common (imitating household appliances), and also the starling's Common and Rare.
issues.suggestion: 'Can count to six and name every colour, so it always knows exactly how many biscuits you hid, and where.' (real research)

issues.issue: 'Wordhoarder' does not fit either the old or the new Rare.
issues.suggestion: 'Biscuitcounter'

issues.issue: Same premise as African grey U (repeats embarrassing words in front of guests).
issues.suggestion: 'Taught every parrot in the pet shop to shout SHOP! at once. The owner has run to the counter four hundred times today.'

issues.issue: Squawking from your shoulder repeats the pirate-shoulder Legendary.
issues.suggestion: 'Chews every pencil, remote and wooden spoon in the house into neat little splinters.'

issues.issue: 'Pirate Pal' describes the Legendary, not the Rare (fake 'who's there?').
issues.suggestion: 'Knockknocker'

issues.issue: The doorbell imitation is the same premise as its own Common and as African grey R.

issues.issue: Same murmuration premise as the Epic.
issues.suggestion: 'Copied the ice-cream van tune so perfectly that every child on the estate ran outside. The van is thinking about a new song.'

issues.issue: 'Organised every crow in town into a gang' shares its frame with raven E ('Organised every raven in the city into a group').

issues.issue: 'Talkacorn' is confusing (acorn?) and does not suggest copying words.

issues.issue: 'Feathers so bright that people think it was painted' is the same as indigo bunting C.

issues.issue: Eating so many bees that flowers must pollinate themselves is a gloomy ecology note, and it repeats the bee-catching in the Common, Rare and Epic.
issues.suggestion: 'Flew in from Africa every summer for so long that the bees started arriving a week late on purpose.'

issues.issue: Weak consequence ('the statue has never been so busy'), plus the 'Led every X' template.

issues.issue: Its singing wakes the whole neighbourhood, which overlaps blackbird L (the town's bedtime song); 'out of business' is a stock punchline.

issues.issue: A four-in-the-morning dawn chorus duplicates seagull R (four in the morning) and the approved smoke detector line.
issues.suggestion: 'Starts the dawn chorus before the milk float, and expects the whole street to join in.'

issues.issue: No punchline: a list of bowl ornaments. 'In the land' is a repeated frame.
issues.suggestion: 'Lived forty years in the same bowl, outlasting three castles and two plastic divers, and is still surprised by the castle.' (callback to the Common)

issues.issue: 'Goldfin' sits close to a famous film villain's name.
issues.suggestion: 'Captain Bubbles of the Fishbowl' (or keep)

issues.issue: 'Mimic Dive' means nothing for a plain diving hit.
issues.suggestion: 'Grey Dive'

issues.issue: A fact with no joke.
issues.suggestion: 'Is the biggest fish in the ocean but only eats the tiniest things in it. Its dinner plate would be a thimble.'

issues.issue: No punchline ('the sea turned a little clearer').
issues.suggestion: 'Swam so slowly past the dive boat that the divers had lunch, a nap and a second dive before its tail went by.'

issues.issue: Singing in the Common, Rare, Epic and Legendary; give one rarity another trait.
issues.suggestion: 'Is so yellow that the miners kept it as a lucky charm, and it now refuses to go anywhere without a tiny helmet.'

issues.issue: Commanding the covey repeats the Uncommon; no punchline.
issues.suggestion: 'Crossed the whole sea at night in one flock, and the lighthouse keeper counted them instead of sheep and slept for a week.'

issues.issue: Confusing: why doorbells?
issues.suggestion: 'Came back from history and keeps trying to pay for things with very old coins.'

issues.issue: Mild extinction joke ('extinct display'). Acceptable, but watch the tone.
issues.suggestion: Keep, or: 'Waddled into the museum and stood very still next to its own statue. Nobody has spotted the difference.'

issues.issue: Fast ocean travel repeats the Rare (beat the cargo ship).
issues.suggestion: 'Swam across a whole ocean in a few weeks, then turned round because it forgot to lock the reef.'

issues.issue: 'The farmer thinks he's going mad' is a mental-health phrase; 'the farmer' also repeats across batches.
issues.suggestion: 'Gobbled at the farmyard until every animal gobbled back. The farmer now answers the phone with a gobble.'

issues.issue: The tail display dominates the Rare, Epic and Legendary.
issues.suggestion: 'Screamed HELP so convincingly from the garden wall that the fire brigade came twice. It was only saying good morning.' (real call)

issues.issue: Slipping between waters in the Uncommon and Rare.
issues.suggestion: 'Changes colour from glassy to yellow to silver as it grows up, and complains every time its clothes stop fitting.' (real life stages)

issues.issue: 'Sent a thank-you card' also appears in limpkin and in w01/w02.
issues.suggestion: 'Powered an underwater research station for a month without being asked. The scientists named the plug socket after it.'

issues.issue: The linter flags cosmic scale below Legendary ('the sun had gone in').
issues.suggestion: 'Spread its wings across the harbour, and every boat thought a cloud had parked overhead.'

issues.issue: 'Charged the owls rent' repeats the rent idea in anemone U and coral U.
issues.suggestion: 'Drilled a perfect round window in the old oak, and the owls moved in before it had finished the curtains.'

issues.issue: 'Four in the morning' is also in bird R.
issues.suggestion: 'Screams from the rooftop before dawn so the whole seaside town wakes before the fishing boats.'
